chapters.title: My Python review notes
chapters.summary: Add your own focused practice questions here.
chapters.lesson: A tuple fixes its sequence of references, but the objects it contains can still be mutable. A tuple containing a list does not make that list immutable. Ask whether an operation changes the tuple itself or an object referenced by it.
chapters.exercise: Create a tuple holding a dictionary. Add a key to the dictionary, then try replacing the dictionary through the tuple's index. Explain the difference.

questions.prompt: Which value is printed after updating the dictionary held in this tuple?
questions.explanation: The dictionary is mutable, so its value can be updated. The tuple still refers to the same dictionary; no tuple element is being replaced.
